data.narrative:
Revel, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Scott Morton, has raised $180M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private robotics companies and one public comparable, providing two independent triangulation methods.

The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $180M total raised as a valuation proxy, yielding $342M. The peer-median approach uses three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—with a median valuation of $1.8B and range of $1.6B to $2.0B. These methods produce significantly divergent signals, reflecting either meaningful stage-specific valuation dispersion within robotics manufacturing or differences in growth trajectory and market positioning among peers.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $291M to $2.0B, with a median of $1.0B. This wide band reflects the substantial gap between the stage-progression and peer-median approaches. Key uncertainties include whether Revel's capital efficiency and burn rate align more closely with earlier-stage profiles or with the higher-funded peer set, and the degree to which peer valuations reflect recent market repricing in frontier robotics. Resolution of valuation within this range depends on assessment of revenue traction, unit economics, and competitive positioning relative to named peers.
